This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation on account of death of Rizwan in the road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, are as follows:
On 01.02.2021 at about 18.00 to 18.01 p.m. Rizwan was proceeding by riding the bicycle, when he reached near 3rd main Chamarajpet and 1st cross, Chamarajpet junction, Bengaluru city, at that time the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596 which was at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner without observing any traffic rules and regulations dashed against the cycle of the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to the impact the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and died on the spot.
Thereafter postmortem was conducted at KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru and handed over the body to the petitioners.
At the time of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 50 years and he was working as Security Guard at EAGLE Detective Security Services Ltd. and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically, they have lost their bread earner.

sentences.text: The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and respondent No.3 are the sisters of the deceased, have lost their beloved care taker.

The respondent No.1 is the insurer,
respondent No.2 is the owner of offending vehicle are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest.
3.
After service of notices the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsels and filed separate written statement.
The respondent No.1 insurance company has filed its written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596.
It is contended that there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of MA Act.
Further it has contended that, the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596 was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also the involvement of the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-MN- 5596 in the alleged accident.
Further it has denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased and also relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is too excessive, exorbitant.
Accordingly, respondent No.1 insurer prays to dismiss the petition against it.
The respondent No.2-owner of the offending vehicle has filed written statement by denying all the petition averments.
Further he has contended that he is the registered owner of the offending vehicle and it is insured with the 1st respondent as on the date of alleged accident.
By denying the alleged fact of negligence and manner in which the petitioners stated about the accident respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against him.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Rizwan died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.02.2021 at about 6.00 p.m. at 3rd main, Chamarajpet,
1st cross, Chamarajpet junction, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent act of driving of Car bearing No.KA-05- MN-5596 by its driver?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased ?
3.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum ? from whom?
4.
What order or award?

Further the petitioners examined one witness as PW2 and got Lakshmamma Alias Lakshmi Alias Bhanu vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67850476/

6.
Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the evidence that is available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1: In the affirmative,

 REASONS ISSUE NO.1;
8.

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint, further statement spot mahazar along with spot sketch, charge sheet, IMV report, PM report and inquest report, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.
9.

As per the documents produced by the petitioner Ex.P1- FIR is came to be registered on the basis of first information and statement given by one Banu who is the sister of the deceased/respondent No.3.
In the said complaint, the first informant alleged the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05- MN-5596.
After registration of FIR the IO has prepared spot mahazar as per Ex.P4 and spot sketch as per Ex.P5.

On perusal of the contents of Ex.P4 and P.5 spot mahazar and sketch it is found that the accident spot is in the middle of the road and while the deceased was proceeding in the bicycle the driver of Car baring No. KA- 05-MN-5596 dashed against the said motor cycle.

It is very important note that as per Ex.P5 sketch the deceased has crossed major portion of the road in his bicycle but the driver of Car baring No. KA-05-MN-5596 were by driving his car in rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased.
It is to be noted that the deceased was in bicycle but the driver of the Car baring No. KA-05-MN-5596 was rash and negligent as such he dashed against the deceased.
If the driver of Car baring No. KA-05-MN-5596 was in a controllable speed and if he was not rash and negligent he could have controlled his car before dashing the deceased.

10. Further Ex.P7 is the IMV report wherein the Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596 has got no fresh visible damages as the deceased was riding the bicycle and the offending vehicle is car which is heavy vehicle, no damages can be expected on the offending car.

Thereby the contents of spot mahazar and sketch prima facie establishes the negligence of the driver of Car bearing Lakshmamma Alias Lakshmi Alias Bhanu vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67850476/

sentences.text: The Ex.P6 is the charge sheet was came to be filed against the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-MN- 5596 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC wherein the IO after detailed investigation has found that there is a negligence on the part of driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596 for the accident.
No other grounds and independent evidence are produced by the respondent No.1 and 2 to prove the contrary to the opinion of the IO as per Ex.P6 charge sheet.
12. The respondent No.1 - insurance company has examined its official as RW.2 who has given evidence on the basis of the police documents and never witnessed the accident.

As such no evidence is available to disbelieve the alleged negligence of the driver of Car baring No. KA-05-MN-5596.
13.
The fact of accident is established before this tribunal.

The Ex.P8 postmortem report and Ex.P9 inquest also establishes that the deceased Rizwan died due to the head injury sustained by him in the said RTA dated 01.02.2021.
14.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: 15. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596 resulting in the death of one Rizwan by sustaining injuries.
Therefore Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
16.
As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Rizwan died on 01.02.2021 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596.

sentences.text: As contended in the petition, that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 & respondent No.3 are the sisters of the deceased.
The respondent No.3-sister of the deceased came on record claiming that she is also dependent on the deceased.
In this regard she has examined herself as RW1 and produced photographs at Ex.R.2.
The petitioners not denied the relationship of respondent No.3 with the deceased but the respondent No.3 disputed the relationship of the petitioner No.1 with the deceased.
Thus the two points arises here for consideration.

Firstly the petitioners should establishes that petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, secondly the petitioner No.2 and respondent No.3 being the sisters of the deceased are also entitled for the compensation.

sentences.text: Coming to the defence of respondent No.1 insurance company that, it has denied the relationship of petitioner No.1 with the deceased.
The crux of the defence of the respondent No.1 is that, the petitioners have made attempt to claim a unknown body and tried to unjustly enriched themselves by usurping the insurance amount.
The whole anchorage of the defence of the respondent No.1 is on the bed rock that there is no relationship whatsoever of the claimants with that of the deceased.

When this being specific positive assertions made by the respondent No.1 insurance company, the onus of proof U/s.102 of Indian Evidence Act shifts back on the claimants to establish their relationship and dependency with that of the deceased.
20. In order to establish the factum of relationship it is relevant to fall back on the documentary proof submitted by the petitioners herein.
The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.1 at Ex.P.13.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, the name of the husband of he petitioner No.1 is shown as Shankaraiah.
But the name of the deceased is Rizwan.
In this regard the petitioner No.1 stated that her first husband Shankaraiah died 30 years back and after the death of said Shankaraiah she has married the Rizwan.
In this regard she has produced Ex.P11 ESI Identity certificate wherein the present petitioner No.1 Lakshmi is shown as spouse.
The Ex.P11 and 12 also contains the joint photograph of the petitioner No.1 and deceased Rizwan.
By producing these documents the petitioner No.1 is trying to establish that she is the wife of the deceased Rizwan.
21. The son of the petitioner No.1 is also examined as PW2 who deposed that after the death of his father Shankaraiah his mother married to Rizwan.

Another witness by name Smt. Vijayamma @
Mumtaz who is the sister of the deceased also examined herself as PW3 who deposed that the said petitioner No.1 has married the deceased and petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
22. It is very important to note that Ex.P.17 statement given by the petitioner No.1 before the IO.
The said statement was given by PW1 at the time of inquest of the body of the deceased.
In the said Ex.P.17 it is clearly stated that the PW1 has married Rizwan after the death of her first husband Shankaraiah in 2001.
Further the Ex.P.18 is the dead body receiving receipt which shows that after the postmortem on 02.02.2021 the body of the deceased was received by petitioner No.1 Lakshmamma.
The Ex.P.18 also establishes that the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
The photographs appended to Ex.P.18 also shows that the body of deceased Rizwan was handed over to petitioner No.1.
These documents establishes that the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.

23. Another important document which is a base for establishing the relationship of the claimants with that of the deceased is that the statement of the petitioner No.2 before the IO at the time of inquest i.e., Ex.P.15.
The Ex.P.15 establishes three points.
Firstly the petitioner No.2 is the sister of the deceased and she is a widow.
Secondly the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
Lastly the petitioner No.2 being the widow was dependent on the deceased who was her brother.
These documents establishes that the petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner No.2 being the widow sister of the deceased was dependent on the deceased.
The documents marked at Ex.P.15, 17 and 18 helped the petitioners to establish their dependency and relationship with the deceased.

Further on dissection of the said document with astuteness it could be culled out that this document was prepared way back from the accident and death of Rizwan which means to say much prior to the date of accident as such this documents cannot be distrusted.

25. Even though the respondent No.1 disputed the relationship of petitioner No.1 and 2 with the deceased nothing substantive proof has been produced by the respondent No.1 herein to disbelieve the evidence of Ex.P11 and 12.
In the absence of which, the said documents cannot be distrusted.

26. The golden thread which runs throughout the case of the claimants is that at the time of inquest the petitioner No.1 identified as a wife and the petitioner No.2 is identified as a sister of the deceased.
The criminal record also discloses that the petitioner No.1 and 2 being the wife and widow sister of the deceased were the dependents of the deceased.
The petitioner No.1 and 2 being the wife and widow sister examined before this tribunal as PW1 and 2 .
In their chief- examination they have deposed with regard to the relationship of the deceased with that of the claimants herein.
When they were subjected to litmus test of cross examination much attach was made in order to impeach their credibility in trying to establish that there is no relationship with the deceased.
Apart from futile attempts made by the respondent No.1 counsel there is absolutely nothing worthwhile was placed on record to distrust the version of PW.1 and 3.
Further, PW.2 is identified as   at the time of the inquest mahazar and his statement is available along with inquest report.
The PW2 also deposed with regard to the relationship of the deceased with that of the claimants.
Though he was cross examined by the respondent No.1 counsel but nothing worthwhile has been elicited in order to distrust the version of PW.2.
The evidence of PW.2 and 3 is relevant u/s 32(5) and Sec. 50 of Indian Evidence Act.
27. Now it is relevant to dwell into conceptual aspects with regard to these provisions of law.
Under clause (5) of Section, a statement relating to the existence of any relationship between the persons alive or dead, is declared as relevant.
But that person making the statement must have special means of knowledge.

Four conditions are to be satisfied for the application of clause (5) of Section 32.
(1) The statement must relate to the existence of any relationship by blood, marriage or adoption.
(2) The person making the statement must have special means of knowledge about the relationship.
(3) The statement must have been made before the question in dispute was raised.
(4) One of the four conditions namely, that a person who is dead, etc., is contained in the main provisions of Section 32.

With regard to Section 50 of Indian Evidence Act:
This section states that when the court has to form an opinion as to the relationship of one person to another, the opinion expressed by conduct by any person who, as a Lakshmamma Alias Lakshmi Alias Bhanu vs National Ins Co Ltd on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67850476/
8 member of the family, or otherwise, has special means of knowledge on the subject, is relevant as to the existence of such relationship.

sentences.text:
Two things are necessary to make the evidence of a witness relevant under this section:-
(1) the witness must have special means of knowledge with regard to existence of the disputed relationship, either as a member of a family, or otherwise; and (2) the witness must depose to his own conduct towards the person whose relationship is in dispute;
The opinion may be of member of the family or an outsider, but he must have special means of knowledge.
28. Reverting back to the factual matrix the PW.3 is the sister of deceased who deposed the petitioner No.1 as the wife of the deceased.
The evidence of PW3 is relevant u/s 50 of Indian Evidence Act.
Without their being any contradictory proof by the respondent No.1 the version of PW.1 to 3 has to be trusted.
Yet another string of evidence which gains a little importance having regard to the factual matrix is the ESI documents and photographs available in Ex.P.11 and 12.
When this court viewed other documentary proof in the light of these documents it is crystal clear and it is clearly forthcoming that there is relationship between the deceased and claimants herein.
29. This Court will not loose sight of the fact that, the petitioners are the dependents of the deceased.
The evidence discloses that deceased is the husband of petitioner No.1 and brother of petitioner No.2 who is a widow and was dependent on her brother.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased and were the dependents on the deceased.
30. Coming to the claim of the respondent No.3, the respondent No.3 being the another sister of the deceased claims that even she was the dependent on the deceased.
The respondent No.3 examined herself as RW1 and produced aadhaar card and photographs in support of her claim.
In the cross-examination she admitted that the deceased was residing with petitioner No.1 and along with petitioner No.1 she has done the last rites of the deceased.
In her cross-examination RW1 admitted that she has a son by name Wasim Pasha.
31. The respondent No.1 insurance company also denied the dependency of respondent No.3 on the deceased.
But on perusal of Ex.P1 FIR and Ex.P.2 complaint, the complaint was given by the respondent No.3.
Whether the sister of the deceased can be dependent has to be looked into.
In this regard the learned counsel for respondent No.3 relied on the following judgments in support of the claim of the respondent No.3.

In that view of the matter, the claimants have a right to maintain a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act,

8. In the instant case, there are no Class I legal heirs to the deceased- Shivanna.
The claimants are the brothers and sisters who will come as Class II legal heirs under the Hindu Succession Act.
Therefore, the petition filed by the claimants was maintainable before the Tribunal.
9. In the circumstances, we are not in a position to accept the argu-ments advanced by the learned Counsel for the K.S.R.T.C.

Accordingly, we hold that the petition filed by the claimants was maintainable before the Tribunal and that they are entitled for compensation.

In this case it is stated that the respondent No.3 being the sister was also dependent on the deceased.
In the complaint marked at Ex.P.2 itself it is stated that the deceased was used to visit the house of the respondent No.3 and was in a cordial relationship with the respondent No.3.
The evidence available on record shows that the respondent No.3 has performed the last rites of the deceased.
Thus, she being the sister also dependent on the deceased, but her dependency will be varies comparing to the petitioner No.1 wife and petitioner No.2 another widow sister.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative by holding the petitioner No.1 and 2 and respondent No.3 are the dependents of the deceased.

As held herein above, the petitioners and respondent No.3 proved that Rizwan died on 01.02.2021 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596.
35.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
The petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased marked at Ex.P13 - as per the said documents the date of birth of the deceased is 06.05.1971, the accident took place 01.02.2021.
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 50 years.
In Ex.P8 postmortem and Ex.P9 inquest the age of the deceased is shown as 50 years.
Hence the age of the petitioner is considered as 50 years.
36. As stated in the petition deceased was working as Security Guard at EGLE Detective Security Services Ltd. and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have produced certificate issued by EGLE Detective Security Services Ltd., Identity certificate and ESI entry book marked at Ex.P10 to P.12.
But they have not produced any salary slips or bank statement to prove the income of the deceased.
No evidence is available to consider what was the exact income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of the evidence the notional income of Rs.15,000/- is considered as the accident is of the year 2021.
37. As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 13.

Since the deceased left his wife and two sisters it is considered that, there are three dependents of deceased,
hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.15,60,000/- (Rs. 15,000/- X 12 X 13 = Rs.23,40,000/- minus 1/3rd (Rs.7,80,000/- =
Rs. 15,60,000/-).

38. In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

The petitioners being the wife, and sisters of the deceased are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each (Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium.

Further, I inclined to award a sum of Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 15,60,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 1,56,000/-
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000/-
4. Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
5. Transportation of dead body Rs. 16,500/-
Total Rs. 18,81,000/-
42. Liability:-
According to the petitioners the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the said vehicle.
Further contended that, the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596 was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident.
But the respondent No.1 has not produced any evidence to prove the same.

Thereby as there was valid policy as on the date of accident and as there was no violation of policy conditions the respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners along with interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly Issue No.3 is answered in the affirmative by holding that the petitioners are entitled for the compensation as discussed above.

43.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is very important note that as per Ex.P5 sketch the deceased has crossed major portion of the road in his bicycle but the driver of Car baring No. KA-05-MN-5596 were by driving his car in rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased.
It is to be noted that the deceased was in bicycle but the driver of the Car baring No. KA-05-MN-5596 was rash and negligent as such he dashed against the deceased.
If the driver of Car baring No. KA-05-MN-5596 was in a controllable speed and if he was not rash and negligent he could have controlled his car before dashing the deceased.
The Ex.P6 is the charge sheet was came to be filed against the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-MN- 5596 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC wherein the IO after detailed investigation has found that there is a negligence on the part of driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-MN-5596 for the accident.
The fact of accident is established before this tribunal.
The Ex.P8 postmortem report and Ex.P9 inquest also establishes that the deceased Rizwan died due to the head injury sustained by him in the said RTA dated 01.02.2021.
14.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.
The respondent No.3-sister of the deceased came on record claiming that she is also dependent on the deceased.
The petitioners not denied the relationship of respondent No.3 with the deceased but the respondent No.3 disputed the relationship of the petitioner No.1 with the deceased.
Firstly the petitioners should establishes that petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, secondly the petitioner No.2 and respondent No.3 being the sisters of the deceased are also entitled for the compensation.
The whole anchorage of the defence of the respondent No.1 is on the bed rock that there is no relationship whatsoever of the claimants with that of the deceased.
When this being specific positive assertions made by the respondent No.1 insurance company, the onus of proof U/s.102 of Indian Evidence Act shifts back on the claimants to establish their relationship and dependency with that of the deceased.
20. In order to establish the factum of relationship it is relevant to fall back on the documentary proof submitted by the petitioners herein.
In the absence of which, the said documents cannot be distrusted.
When they were subjected to litmus test of cross examination much attach was made in order to impeach their credibility in trying to establish that there is no relationship with the deceased.

Without their being any contradictory proof by the respondent No.1 the version of PW.1 to 3 has to be trusted.
29. This Court will not loose sight of the fact that, the petitioners are the dependents of the deceased.
